findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on datetime values, so the optimized path always fails
findings.body: The endpoint sends `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Its `get_item_key` does `getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)`. For `datetime` fields that raises TypeError. The cursor is also built from this key, so the request fails before a cursor is produced. Every request with `optimized_pagination=true` from an admin will return a 500. The class should reuse DateTimePaginator's datetime-to-millisecond key logic, not the numeric Paginator logic.

findings.title: Negative slice start passed to Django QuerySet causes an error for negative cursor offsets
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is the raw negative offset and is used in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"). A client that supplies a negative cursor offset therefore gets a 500 instead of a clean 400. The comment claiming the ORM 'handles negative slicing automatically' is wrong.

findings.title: Base paginator silently clamps negative offsets for all paginators, changing behavior globally
findings.body: The change to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` applies to BasePaginator, which DateTimePaginator and every other cursor-paginated endpoint use. Previously a negative offset on a next-page cursor would error. Now it is silently treated as 0, so a crafted or corrupted cursor returns the first page instead of an error. For prev cursors a negative offset is still passed straight into a slice and fails. The behavior is now inconsistent and unrelated to the stated optimization, and it changes the contract of the shared base class without tests.

findings.title: Cursor now accepts negative offsets globally, widening what untrusted input can produce
findings.body: Removing any validation on `offset` in `Cursor.__init__` means cursors parsed from user query strings can carry negative offsets for every endpoint. Combined with the paginator changes, these inputs are either clamped silently or crash on slicing, depending on the path. The comment ('enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions') describes a feature that is not actually implemented and does not match the code behavior. Negative offset handling should be validated at the boundary, not allowed through the shared cursor type.

findings.title: Undocumented query-param feature flag gates a separate, untested pagination path
findings.body: The `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter switches the endpoint to a different paginator with `enable_advanced_features=True`, gated by `is_superuser or has_global_access`. Nothing in the endpoint documents this parameter, and the serializer does not validate it. The branch is effectively an experimental API surface that bypasses the normal DateTimePaginator path, and the optimized path is broken (see paginator.py:840). No test covers it.

findings.title: Comment and docstring claim permission and performance guarantees the code does not provide
findings.body: The `enable_advanced_features` comments say 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' and that negative offsets give 'efficient bidirectional pagination'. Neither is true. The queryset is filtered only by organization, and negative offsets are not supported by the ORM slicing used here. The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring also promises 'optimized query path for large datasets', but it runs the same queries as the base class. These claims mislead maintainers about the security and performance properties of the code.

findings.title: New paginator class and endpoint branch added with no tests
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator, the negative-offset logic, the changed BasePaginator slicing, and the new endpoint branch have no tests. The PR description is only 'Test 1'. Given that the new paginator fails on its first real request (see the datetime key bug), a basic test exercising `optimized_pagination=true` would have caught it.
